episode.tagline: The road from desire to action is long & painful. How can we make it a smooth journey?
episode.about: In this episode, Amit shares his learnings on productivity, beginning with the inspiring story of a young Goan boy, speechless in a grand hall in Lisbon in the 18th century, finding his wits when his father hisses at him -- and at us -- the greatest productivity mantra ever: Kaator Re Bhaaji. Amit explains what this means, and shares a set of productivity tips. Ajay zooms out and talks about the importance of purpose. He also delivers a passionate tribute to Unix!

items.content: Ajay opens the episode: 'we are at the brink of a great moment in merchandising where the slogan just do it is going to be overpowered…
Amit on Faria's parents being a priest and a nun: 'don't worry, no hanky panky', since they joined the church after having him.
Amit's dramatic scene-setting in Lisbon: 'an August gathering, though I don't know if it was August', with royalty 'in their breeches…
Ajay dates Faria's birth in 1756 as 'before the Battle of Plassey', and Amit replies, 'There you go.'
In the pottery experiment, the planning group gets to take online courses in 'the art of clear pottery', a nod to Amit's writing course,…
Amit describing a dying reading habit: 'somebody is wrong on the internet, and obviously I have to correct them', after which you decide…
Amit on owning your identity as a reader: at friends' houses 'the first thing I will check out is their bookshelves. Only then will I…
Amit on no one watching you: 'No one is taking screenshots and waiting to put it on Twitter to shame you, or actually in my case, they are.'
After Amit's first slogan, Ajay says: 'Very well, Amit. Now contradict yourself.' Amit replies, 'I will contradict myself for we contain…
Abraham Lincoln's line, quoted by Amit, about spending five of six hours sharpening the axe before chopping the tree. Amit then admits…
Rodin and The Thinker: he didn't conjure it from thin air but 'edited the block of stone', which is Amit's picture of a first draft.
Ajay: 'the problem with practical goals is that you'll actually achieve them.' Amit: 'It's like the dog that chases a car and finally…
A line Amit attributes to either Christopher Hitchens or Richard Dawkins: believers are atheists about the thousands of other religions,…
Ajay mentions GTD and Amit replies, 'You're scaring the shit out of me. What is GTD?'
Ajay dislikes the word productivity because 'it's too much of a managerial thing. It's too much Taylorism for me.'
After Ajay criticises academics chasing 'pubs', Amit says: 'it is not only academics who want pubs. I was once in Europe, it was a hot…
Amit's fantasy of building one app to replace Roam, Notion, Final Draft and Scrivener: 'maybe I can do it one day and I'll get GPT-4 or…
Donald Knuth calls TeX 'my Taj Mahal' and sends cheques to anyone who finds a bug. The finders frame them instead of cashing them.
Asked who was the greatest man of the last fifty years, Ajay picked Ken Thompson, crediting his values and aesthetic sense for the Unix…
Amit after Ajay's Unix tribute: 'What does a Marathi programmer say to another Marathi programmer when he finds a flaw in a computer…
Amit teasing Ajay for skipping last week's recommendation: 'You weren't prepared, which is a great flaw in your productivity processes,…
Amit calls the YouTube audience 'gentle readers', and Ajay approves: 'Good old-fashioned 19th century speak.'
Roam Research is based on Zettelkasten, which Amit describes as a German note-taking system.
